statement: Alphabet funded its 2Q26 build-out with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of senior unsecured notes, and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion.
why: When even the best-capitalized buyer turns to equity and debt markets and runs negative free cash flow, the pace of AI buying starts to depend on financing conditions rather than operating cash alone.

impact.mechanism: External funding sustains the current buying pace but ties future accelerator and data-center orders to continued access to cheap capital, a fragility if credit conditions tighten.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance (Bloomberg wire) — "Google increases capex forecast again after cloud-driven earnings beat"
evidence.excerpt: Alphabet raised $49.6 billion through equity issuance in June and obtained $20.3 billion via senior unsecured notes in Q2.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance (Bloomberg wire) — "Google increases capex forecast again after cloud-driven earnings beat"
evidence.excerpt: first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion that quarter.

confidence.basis: Single secondary wire report; figures are specific but not drawn from the filing itself and not corroborated across separately fetched publishers.
